# Test differences in alpha diversity trajectories over time by abx use group
## Read and format data

```{r read.data.factor, include=FALSE}
long_df = read.csv('../data/stool_repeat_clients_long.csv',
                  colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))

# Want to make sure that categorical vars are factored properly
long_df$sex <- factor(long_df$sex)
long_df$meds_blood_sugar <- factor(long_df$meds_blood_sugar)
long_df$meds_cholesterol <- factor(long_df$meds_cholesterol)
long_df$abx_recency <- factor(long_df$abx_recency)
long_df$vendor_dashboard <- factor(long_df$vendor_dashboard)

# Let's mean center our age and GFR
# redoing GFR because the slice of the data may be different
long_df$centered_age <- long_df$age - mean(long_df$age)
```

```{r check.abx.ref, include=FALSE}
levels(long_df$abx_recency) # Checking the "none" abx is the reference
```

```{r decompose.bmi}
long_df$bmi_person_mean = ave(long_df$BMI_CALC, # For column BMI
                      long_df$public_client_id, # Group by person
                      FUN = mean) 

# To find person-specific deviation of a particular time point
long_df$bmi_within = (long_df$BMI_CALC -        # For each time point
                      long_df$bmi_person_mean)  # Subtract person-mean


# To compare from person to person 
long_df$bmi_between = scale(long_df$bmi_person_mean, # Subtract grand-mean from person-mean
                            scale=FALSE)             # Do not z-score
```

```{r create.time.window.var}
long_df$time_100 <- long_df$dsb / 100
```

```{r set.up.models}
outcomes = c('observed_features','berger_parker','shannon_index')

time_by_abx = 'time_100*abx_recency'       # Use for interaction models
time_plus_abx = 'time_100 + abx_recency'   # Remove interaction for LRT

covars_no_time = c('centered_age', 'sex', 'meds_blood_sugar', 'meds_cholesterol', 'PC1',
                   'PC2', 'PC3', 'PC4', 'PC5', 'centered_eGFR', 'vendor_dashboard',
                   'bmi_within', 'bmi_between')
```

## Run models with interaction

Going to try running the model with observed features to get a hang of model
specification.

```{r model.obs.test}
mod_obs <- lmer(observed_features ~ time_100*abx_recency + sex + centered_age + 
                  meds_blood_sugar + meds_cholesterol + centered_eGFR + 
                  PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + vendor_dashboard + bmi_within + 
                  bmi_between + (1 | public_client_id),
             data=long_df)

summary(mod_obs)
```

```{r check.icc}
icc(mod_obs)
```
Looks like around 70% of the variation is between people, so using the random intercept
is helpful!

### Vectorized below

```{r run.int.models}
models_interaction <- setNames(lapply(outcomes, function(outcome) {
  fixed_terms <- c(time_by_abx, covars_no_time)
  formula <- reformulate(fixed_terms, response = outcome)
  mod <- lmer(update(formula, . ~ . + (1|public_client_id)), # Create model
              data = long_df)
  attr(mod, "outcome") <- outcome # Attach outcome name to the model
  mod                             # Return the model object
  }), 
  outcomes)                       # Names the list index (uses setNames)
  
# formula(models_interaction$observed_features) # Used to see which formula was used
```

## Run models without interaction

```{r run.add.models}
models_additive <- setNames(lapply(outcomes, function(outcome) {
  fixed_terms <- c(time_plus_abx, covars_no_time)
  formula <- reformulate(fixed_terms, response = outcome)
  mod <- lmer(update(formula, . ~ . + (1|public_client_id)), # Create model
              data = long_df)
  attr(mod, "outcome") <- outcome # Attach outcome name to the model
  mod                             # Return the model object
  }), 
  outcomes)                       # Names the list index (uses setNames)
```

## Perform LRT

```{r lrt.all.alphas}
LRT_pvals <- setNames(sapply(outcomes, function(outcome) {
  anova(
    models_additive[[outcome]],
    models_interaction[[outcome]]
  )$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
}), outcomes)

LRT_pvals
```

```{r FDR.adjustment}
# Extract just the numbers
pvals_num <- unlist(LRT_pvals)   
qvals <- p.adjust(pvals_num, method = "BH")

results_lmm_alphas <- data.frame(
  name = names(pvals_num),
  p_value = pvals_num,
  q_value = qvals
)

results_lmm_alphas
```

Awesome, looks like all of these meet q<0.1, suggesting that having the interaction
between the time*group variable (i.e., different slopes for the antibiotic users)
was helpful in modeling the data. This may suggest that the recovery trajectory 
was different between the antibiotic use groups. Let's go ahead and look at the data
some more. 

## Interpretation

```{r print.formula}
formula(models_interaction$observed_features)
```

```{r get.estimates}
models_interaction$observed_features
```
Looks like the average person in the reference/none group showed a slight
decrease in the number of observed features over time. In particular, it's a decrease
of -0.29 features over a period of 100 days. However, the individuals in the 
antibiotic groups have a different slope.

- **Three month group:**  -0.2916 + 1.1888  = 0.8972
- **Twelve month group:** -0.2916 + 0.4788  = 0.1872

In all cases, the magnitude of the change is quite small, but it is interesting
that the change is greatest/most positive for the 3 month group.

```{r}
summary(models_interaction$observed_features)
``` 

## Let's plot it!

```{r spaghetti.plot.draft}
# ggplot(long_df,

#          color=abx_recency)) +
```

```{r obtain.emm}
emm <- emmeans(models_interaction$observed_features, ~ abx_recency | time_100,
               at = list(time_100 = seq(min(long_df$time_100), # evaluate between
                                        max(long_df$time_100),
                                        length.out = 50))) # 50 time points

emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm)
```

```{r plot.emm}
ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = time_100, y = emmean, color = abx_recency)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.3) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL, fill = abx_recency),
              alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Okay let's put these together!

```{r composite.plot, fig.width=5, fig.height=5}
ggplot() +
  # raw data
  geom_point(data = long_df,
            aes(x = time_100,
                y = observed_features,
                group = public_client_id,
                color = abx_recency),
            alpha = 0.5) +
  
  geom_line(data = long_df,
            aes(x = time_100,
                y = observed_features,
                group = public_client_id,
                color = abx_recency),
            alpha = 0.17) +

  # emmeans CI bands
  geom_ribbon(data = emm_df,
              aes(x = time_100, ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL, fill = abx_recency),
              alpha = 0.25) +

  # emmeans lines
  geom_line(data = emm_df,
            aes(x = time_100, y = emmean, color = abx_recency),
            linewidth = 1.5) +
  
    scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "none" = "#007ea7", 
    "twelve" = "#80ced7", 
    "three" = "darkgrey"
  )) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "none" = "#007ea7", 
    "twelve" = "#80ced7", 
    "three" = "darkgrey"
  )) +
  
  labs(x = 'Time since baseline (per 100 days)', y = 'Observed Features') +
  
  #theme_dark()

  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
plot(emm, comparisons = TRUE)
```


## Assess model assumptions

```{r check.VIF}
check_collinearity(models_interaction$observed_features)
```

Now check residuals:

```{r plot.resid.function}
plot_residuals <- function(model) {
  df <- data.frame(
    Fitted = fitted(model),
    Residuals = residuals(model, type = "pearson")
  )
  
  outcome_name <- attr(model, "outcome")
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = Fitted, y = Residuals)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Residuals vs Fitted:", outcome_name),
      x = "Fitted values",
      y = "Pearson residuals"
    ) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size=10, color = "blue"))
}
```


```{r plot.lca.models}
model_list <- models_interaction             # List of LCA models
plots_resids <- lapply(model_list, plot_residuals)  # Individual plots

# Combine plots into a single figure
combined_plot <- plot_grid(plotlist = plots_resids, ncol = 3)

combined_plot # Display
```
